messages.text: Red Roses want to use back-to-back losses to Canada as 'learning opportunity'

metadata.summary: Emma Sing knows England have had a tough run in the WXV Global Series after back-to-back defeats snapped a 41-game winning streak - but is hoping to turn the moment into a learning opportunity.
metadata.content: How England's Red Roses want to use back-to-back losses to Canada in WXV Global Series as 'learning opportunity' | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content How England's Red Roses want to use back-to-back losses to Canada in WXV Global Series as 'learning opportunity' Canada repeated a victory over England in the WXV Global Series, winning 31-22 in Ottawa; England suffer first back-to-back defeats in a decade; first loss to Canada ended a four-year unbeaten run; Emma Sing thinks the team are now building towards the 2029 Rugby World Cup Megan Wellens Sports Journalist @MegWellensX Tuesday 27 October 2026 21:22, UK Image: Emma Sing thinks that the Red Roses are building towards 2029 Emma Sing knows England have had a tough run in the WXV Global Series after back-to-back defeats snapped a 41-game winning streak - but is hoping to turn the moment into a learning opportunity. The successive losses to Canada marked the first time the Red Roses had lost twice in a row in a decade. Not only that, Canada's 24-21 defeat in Toronto, which they backed up in Ottawa, brought their four-year unbeaten run to an end. Red Roses' four-year record gone - but good for women's rugby? messages.text: Carrick to remain in charge of Man Utd for Chelsea trip

metadata.summary: Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday.
metadata.content: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around Man Utd's under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick being given the opportunity to turn current situation around with the 13-time Premier League winners currently on an eight-game winless run in all competitions and one point above the relegation zone Danyal Khan Sky Sports News Reporter @DanyalHKhan Tuesday 27 October 2026 17:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan is at Manchester United's Carrington training ground with the significant news that Michael Carrick will remain in charge heading into the weekend Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday. The under-pressure United head coach was thought to be on the brink after Sunday's crushing 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, but he and the players are being given the chance to turn the current situation around. United's director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, were at Carrington discussing Carrick's future on Monday. It is understood they had already been considering alternatives for the head coach role. However, Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision has been taken to give him at least one more match. metadata.summary: Stuart Broad has blasted Lancashire's decision to not renew James Anderson's contract as "disrespectful".
metadata.content: James Anderson: Stuart Broad blasts Lancashire's 'disrespectful' decision to not renew ex-England bowler contract | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content James Anderson: Stuart Broad blasts Lancashire's 'disrespectful' decision to not renew ex-England bowler contract Stuart Broad said the way in which Lancashire decided not to give James Anderson another contract was "disrespectful"; since his England retirement, Anderson has continued playing for Lancashire and captained the county in Division Two this year Tuesday 27 October 2026 19:22, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Kumar Sangakkara give their thoughts on Lancashire not renewing James Anderson's contract Stuart Broad has blasted Lancashire's decision to not renew James Anderson's contract as "disrespectful". The Red Rose county opted against offering him a new deal for 2027 despite the 44-year-old having a strong season in which he took 50 wickets at an average of 17 amid their struggles in Division Two of the County Championship. Anderson released a statement on social media which confirmed his Lancashire departure was not what he wanted and that if it was up to him, it "would not have ended like this".
